name: SurveyMonkey
summary: Survey and feedback platform: build surveys, collect responses at scale and analyze results for market research, CX and employee feedback. A native Salesforce integration pushes responses straight into Salesforce, triggers workflows off the answers themselves (churn-risk follow-up or an NPS detractor landing on a rep's desk, for instance) and ties feedback back to accounts and pipeline, so sales and CS read it inside the tool they already work in rather than in a separate reporting dashboard.
best_for: teams that need research-grade survey logic (skip logic, randomisation, quotas) with compliance (HIPAA, GDPR, SOC 2) and 200+ integrations
skip_if: you just need a simple form (Google Forms is free) or you're cost-sensitive with high response volumes: the overage fees add up
honest_knock: The free tier is a teaser. Response caps on the self-serve plans trigger $0.15-per-response overages (US rate; Enterprise contracts set their own limits) that become a hidden cost on big studies. Branding and customisation are limited, and a lot of the good analytics and logic sit behind higher tiers.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per user a month, billed annually
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-01 in surveymonkey.com/pricing.md, whose header now dates the content 2026-09-22, and on surveymonkey.com/pricing/ as served to a euro storefront) Team plans are billed annually and need three or more users; pricing.md no longer lists any monthly Team variant. Every Team seat costs the same, the first one included: in the US table Team Advantage Annual is $360 a user a year and Team Premier Annual $1,104, the $30 and $92 a month the SurveyMonkey partner team quoted by email on 24 September 2026, so three seats come to $1,080 or $3,312 a year. Euro storefronts read €360 and €900 a user a year, shown on the page as €30 and €75 a month. The euro pricing page states the included responses: 50,000 a year on Team Advantage and 100,000 on Team Premier, counted across all surveys and users; Enterprise (five or more users, custom quote) has a custom limit. Overage above the limit is priced per storefront: $0.15 a response in dollar countries, €0.10 in euro countries, £0.15 in sterling; SurveyMonkey Audience responses are sold separately. Individual plans in the US table: Standard Monthly $149 a month, Standard Annual $300 a year (US, GB and AU only, not offered to churned Basic users), Advantage Annual $468 and Premier Annual $1,668 a year. The pricing.md edition updated 27 October 2026 (read 12 November 2026) still lists $149 a month for the US. The $99 a month was a partner-team email quote of 24 September 2026 and appears in no published table. The €39 a month we saw at checkout matches the German euro row (the Irish row reads €35), so it is a different storefront, not a different US price. The free Basic plan allows 10 questions per survey, and pricing.md now shows its response limit as 10 outside Canada, where Basic users keep 25.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 5 November 2026 on the free Basic plan: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We drafted a small quiz survey, looked for an export, and opened the checkout for Standard Monthly without paying. We collected no responses and sent nothing.
findings: Sign-up asked four profile questions and then dropped us on the home screen. No card, no sales call and no linked account was required.

The account page shows 'Basic (Free) Account', '10 responses per survey' and 'Survey data storage: United States'. 'Access to Benchmarks' was already switched on, so your survey results feed SurveyMonkey's benchmarks unless you turn it off.

Quiz scoring worked on Basic: we marked one answer as worth one point. A 'Multiple textboxes' question raised the toast '1 paid feature added! Upgrade your plan or remove paid features to send this survey.' Basic lets you preview paid question types, but not send a survey that uses one.
In Analyze results, 'New export' and 'Previous exports' are locked, with the panel 'Good data deserves a way out' and an Upgrade button. On Basic we found no way to export results.

The pricing page opens on Team plans: Team Advantage at €30 per user per month, from 3 users, billed annually. Individual plans sit behind a second tab: Standard Monthly €39 a month, Advantage Annual €36 a month (€432 billed annually), Premier Annual €99 a month (€1,188 billed annually).

Checkout for Standard Monthly, with the Netherlands pre-filled, showed 'Total (VAT included) €39'. The sentence under it says the plan renews at €39 monthly 'plus applicable taxes'. The two statements do not agree, so confirm the tax basis before you buy. We stopped before any payment.
not_tested: Collecting responses and exporting them: Basic gave us no way to submit test responses, so both fictional kit records stayed untested
Round trip with native record IDs; export bytes were never downloaded
Support, team roles, API access and invitations: the Team page asked for a paid plan and we did not open the developer pages
Downgrade and cancellation: we were already on the free plan
How long a full sign-up takes from the first click; Daan created the account before we started counting
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
